Title: Research through Design (RtD)
Short description: MSc Integrated Product Design, TU Delft
Description: Building prototypes to ask questions instead of answering them.
longDescription: In the IPD master at TU Delft I learned to work with research through design: you build something to learn from it, not to deliver it. I made physical prototypes to explore how people respond to objects and interactions. Every version showed me something I would not have found by only thinking about it. It is now how I start most projects: make something rough early, see what it does, and let that steer the next step.

Title: Klimmende Stapelaar
Description: A mechanism that stacks objects by climbing, designed, calculated and built during my bachelor.
longDescription: The assignment was a mechanism that stacks objects by climbing up a vertical structure. I went through the whole route: working out the motion requirements, choosing a mechanism, doing the strength and stiffness calculations, modelling it in CAD and building the prototype. The kinematics worked on paper fairly quickly. Getting the real thing to hold together under load took a lot longer.

Title: Custom Mini Vehicle
Description: A small vehicle built from scratch: chassis, gearing and steering, no kit.
longDescription: I designed and built this vehicle from the ground up, without a kit or standard platform. Chassis, gearing and steering all had to fit in a tiny package and still work together: enough torque to pull away cleanly, and a frame stiff enough to keep the steering predictable. Plenty of parts that looked fine in CAD needed rework once I put them together, and that is where most of the learning happened.

Title: Direct Air Carbon Capture Paper
Description: Could a mechanical direct air capture system work at scale? I ran the numbers on the energy it would need.
longDescription: This paper looked at capturing CO₂ straight from the air with a mechanical system. The question was simple: given the thermodynamics, could it work at a scale that actually matters? I worked through the physics of the capture process, modelled the energy demand at different scales and wrote down what those numbers mean for feasibility. No prototype this time, just analysis and an argument that has to hold up on paper.

Title: Mini CNC Machine
Description: A small 3-axis CNC machine, from frame and linear guides to stepper motors.
longDescription: I designed and built a desktop CNC. It needed a stiff frame, well-supported linear guides on every axis and stepper motors precise enough to cut usable parts. I did the structure and axis layout in CAD, picked the guides and drive parts, built the frame and set up the motion control. Any error in alignment or stiffness showed up straight away in the cut, so it took a few rounds on both the mechanics and the electronics before it ran properly.

Title: Baxter Roll
Description: A product taken from research to a detailed prototype, designed around how it feels to use.
longDescription: Baxter Roll was a full product development project: research, concepts and finally a detailed mechanical design. Besides making it work, I wanted it to feel right in the hand, so ergonomics and materials were part of the design from the start instead of something to fix at the end. I modelled everything in SolidWorks to check how the parts fit before building anything, and went through several prototype rounds.

Title: Hyperion Lyceum
Description: Secondary school with a focus on maths and science, and the route to TU Delft.
longDescription: I did my VWO at Hyperion Lyceum in Amsterdam with a science profile: maths, physics, chemistry and biology. From there, Mechanical Engineering in Delft was the logical next step.

Title: IDE Business Fair
Description: Chaired the committee behind the IDE Business Fair 2026, where design students meet companies.
longDescription: After switching from Mechanical Engineering to Industrial Design Engineering, I wanted to be part of the faculty in more than an academic way. I was asked to chair the Business Fair committee, which was an honour and a lot of fun. I got to talk with a lot of companies, learned how acquisition and leading a team actually work, and made good friends along the way. The event had to raise a four-figure amount, so it also came with real responsibility.

Title: Offshore Workability Analysis
Description: At Ampelmann I check whether offshore walk-to-work operations are feasible, based on weather data, vessel motions and equipment limits.
longDescription: At Ampelmann I work on workability analyses for motion-compensated gangways: the systems that let people walk from a vessel onto an offshore structure when the sea would otherwise make that unsafe. For every planned operation the question is whether it will work with the expected waves and weather, this vessel and these equipment limits. I work with wave and weather data and vessel motion behaviour, and turn that into reports that planners use to decide what happens offshore.

Title: High School STEM Tutoring
Description: One-on-one tutoring and exam prep in maths, physics and chemistry.
longDescription: I tutored secondary school students one-on-one for their maths, physics and chemistry exams. The subject itself was rarely the problem. The real work was figuring out where someone got stuck and finding another way to explain it until it clicked. That is still the part I enjoy most, and it changed how I explain technical things in general.

Title: Platenmeubel (Vinyl Cabinet)
Description: A lasercut wooden cabinet for my turntable and records, with lit glass bricks.
longDescription: A friend told me he was going to make a lamp out of glass bricks. As a true artist, I stole the idea and built it into my record cabinet. I drew the plates in AutoCAD and checked in SolidWorks whether the assembly would fit. Then it went to the not-so-perfect lasercutter, which meant a lot more woodworking than I had planned. Finally I stained the wood to make it look good.

Title: Ergonomic Laptop Stand
Description: A laptop stand that raises the screen and lets air under the laptop.
longDescription: A small project, but I took it seriously. I wanted the screen higher, air under the laptop and something that looks like it belongs on a clean desk. That meant working out the right viewing height while sitting, making it stiff enough not to flex under the laptop, and keeping the shape simple.

Title: Photography
Short description: Light, texture and things you would walk past
Description: Photos of the moments in between, mostly in natural light.
longDescription: For me photography is mostly about paying attention. I am drawn to natural light, textures and small moments that are easy to miss, like a good shadow or two things that happen to line up. I shoot with whatever camera I have and do not try to make the picture perfect. What I take from it into design is the habit of choosing what goes in the frame and what stays out.

Title: Writing & Production
Description: Writing and producing mostly instrumental music, with a lot of attention to arrangement.
longDescription: I write and produce mostly instrumental music, with both recordings and synths. Most of my time goes into arrangement: deciding what needs to be there and, more often, what does not. It works a lot like design. You make something, listen to what it actually does instead of what you meant, and adjust.

Title: BHS
Description: A yearly event where 16 to 18 artists from different disciplines make music, furniture, paintings and photos together.
longDescription: BHS is based on Desert Sessions, the project by Josh Homme where musicians from different bands came together in the desert to make an album. I took that idea and turned it into an event that has happened almost every year since. Around 16 to 18 artists from different backgrounds come together to make music, furniture, paintings, photography, video and whatever else comes up. I organised the first edition on my own. For the later ones I had help from other organisers, which also gave me room to work on my own things. It is great to see people try things they would never do otherwise and get inspired by each other. For me it was a lesson in organising, learning from others and facilitating instead of doing everything yourself.

Title: EasyTabMaker
Description: easytabmaker.com: a free guitar tab editor without ads, with accounts and shareable tabs.
longDescription: I built EasyTabMaker because I could not find a free tab editor that was nice to use. Everything out there was full of ads, too complicated or missing basic features. So I made my own: a clean editor for writing guitar tabs, with accounts so you can save, edit and share them. I built the whole thing, from the interface and front-end to data storage and accounts on the back-end. It is live at easytabmaker.com.
